description: The Financial Stability Report summarises the Federal Reserve Board's framework for assessing the resilience of the US financial system and presents its current assessment. It is produced by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to promote public understanding and increase transparency and accountability for the Fed's views. Coverage is the US financial system. Reports appear twice a year, from November 2018 to the latest in May 2026, each free in HTML and PDF with the chart data and descriptions, and some editions carry statements by Board members. Caveats: the report is an assessment, the chart data come from many public and proprietary sources, and the page read gives no licence statement. For simulation it gives a regular, documented assessment of vulnerabilities, with chart data, that helps calibrate and choose shocks for resilience and cascading failure models of the financial system. It is related to the FSOC annual reports record in this catalogue and to the Federal Reserve stress test scenarios record.
